key_insight: A two-stage machine-learning potential workflow can model how amino-silane passivates hybrid halide perovskite surfaces and how interactions change with molecular coverage.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a practical route to simulate experimentally realistic perovskite surface passivation, helping guide defect-healing strategies for more stable, higher-performance solar cells.
method: Built a large open training set of diverse metal and hybrid halide perovskite structures (hyP-26).
Fine-tuned the model with a small, specialized dataset for an amino-silane molecule on the surface.
Used the resulting potential to probe coverage-dependent collective interactions at a mixed-composition perovskite surface.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a multistep training pipeline and its application to a curated broad dataset plus a targeted passivation dataset, then uses the model to reveal evolving interactions as molecular surface coverage increases.
watch_item: Because the passivation chemistry is highly specific, performance may depend strongly on the quality and representativeness of the fine-tuning dataset.
paper_title: Data-driven atomistic modelling of hybrid halide perovskite passivation
